sections.subtitle: Real Conditions: Si + Present Indicative
sections.content:
✅ REAL CONDITIONS (likely/possible scenarios)

📋 PATTERN:
SI + present indicative, present/future/imperative

💡 With PRESENT result (habitual):
→ Si llueve, no voy
(If it rains, I don't go - regular habit)
→ Si tengo tiempo, leo
(If I have time, I read - usual occurrence)

🔮 With FUTURE result (likely future):
→ Si llueve, no iré
(If it rains, I won't go)
→ Si estudias, aprobarás
(If you study, you'll pass)

📢 With IMPERATIVE (commands):
→ Si ves a Juan, dile hola
(If you see Juan, say hello)

⚠️ CRITICAL RULE:
Never use future tense after SI in Spanish!

❌ WRONG: Si lloverá...
✅ CORRECT: Si llueve...
(Use present tense even for future meaning)

These express OPEN conditions - situations that may actually happen.

sections.subtitle: Future Possibilities & Real Condition Nuances
sections.content:
🔮 FUTURE POSSIBILITIES

SI + present → future in result (very common!):
→ Si hace buen tiempo, iremos a la playa
(If weather is good, we'll go to beach)
→ Si terminas temprano, podremos cenar juntos
(If you finish early, we can dinner together)

🔄 PRESENT in result (habitual/general truths)
→ Si como mucho, me siento mal
(If I eat a lot, I feel bad - always happens)
→ Si el agua llega a 100°, hierve
(If water reaches 100°, it boils - universal truth)

📢 IMPERATIVE in result (commands/instructions)
→ Si tienes frío, ponte un suéter
(If you're cold, put on a sweater)
→ Si no entiendes, pregunta
(If you don't understand, ask)

💡 Remember:
All these use INDICATIVE (not subjunctive) in SI clause
They express real, open possibilities that might actually happen

sections.subtitle: Hypothetical Present: Si + Imperfect Subjunctive
sections.content:
💭 HYPOTHETICAL CONDITIONS (contrary-to-fact/unlikely)

📋 PATTERN:
SI + imperfect subjunctive, conditional

The imperfect subjunctive signals 'this isn't real'

💡 Examples:
→ Si tuviera dinero, compraría un coche
(If I HAD money, I would buy a car)
→ But I don't have money now

→ Si fuera rico, viajaría por el mundo
(If I WERE rich, I would travel the world)
→ But I'm not rich

→ Si pudiera volar, iría a la luna
(If I COULD fly, I would go to the moon)
→ impossible/contrary to reality

🎯 The CONDITIONAL in result = what WOULD happen

→ Si hablara chino, conseguiría ese trabajo
(If I spoke Chinese, I would get that job)
→ But I don't speak Chinese

→ Si vivieras más cerca, te visitaría más
(If you lived closer, I would visit you more)
→ But you don't live close

📚 Common verbs in imperfect subjunctive:
tuviera/tuviese (had)
fuera/fuese (were)
pudiera/pudiese (could)
hiciera/hiciese (did/made)
supiera/supiese (knew)

sections.subtitle: Real vs Hypothetical: Key Distinctions
sections.content:
🎯 UNDERSTANDING THE DIFFERENCE

✅ REAL (present indicative):
→ Si tengo tiempo, voy al cine
(If I have time, I go to the cinema)
→ It's possible I'll have time, this happens sometimes

💭 HYPOTHETICAL (imperfect subjunctive):
→ Si tuviera tiempo, iría al cine
(If I had time, I would go to the cinema)
→ I don't have time, contrary to current reality

🔍 More comparisons:

REAL:
→ Si Juan está aquí, puedo preguntarle
(If Juan is here, I can ask him)
→ He might be here, let me check

HYPOTHETICAL:
→ Si Juan estuviera aquí, podría preguntarle
(If Juan were here, I could ask him)
→ But he's NOT here now

REAL:
→ Si llueve mañana, no iremos
(If it rains tomorrow, we won't go)
→ Realistic possibility

HYPOTHETICAL:
→ Si lloviera en el desierto, crecerían plantas
(If it rained in the desert, plants would grow)
→ Unlikely/imagining different scenario

💡 The choice depends on speaker's view:
possible reality vs imagined/contrary-to-fact

sections.subtitle: Past Hypotheticals: Si + Pluperfect Subjunctive
sections.content:
⏰ PAST HYPOTHETICAL (unreal past)

Express situations that DIDN'T happen - 'what could have been'

📋 PATTERN:
SI + pluperfect subjunctive, conditional perfect

• Pluperfect subjunctive: hubiera/hubiese + past participle
• Conditional perfect: habría + past participle

💡 Examples:

→ Si hubiera estudiado, habría aprobado
(If I HAD studied, I WOULD HAVE passed)
→ But I didn't study, and I didn't pass

→ Si hubieras venido, habrías conocido a María
(If you HAD come, you WOULD HAVE met María)
→ But you didn't come, so you didn't meet her

→ Si hubiéramos salido antes, habríamos llegado a tiempo
(If we HAD left earlier, we WOULD HAVE arrived on time)
→ But we didn't leave earlier, so we were late

😔 Express regret or missed opportunities:

→ Si lo hubiera sabido, no habría ido
(If I had known it, I wouldn't have gone)
→ Regret

→ Si hubiera tenido dinero, habría comprado la casa
(If I had had money, I would have bought the house)
→ Missed opportunity

💭 Common for reflecting on past decisions and their potential outcomes

sections.subtitle: Alternative Conditional Structures
sections.content:
⚠️ COMO + SUBJUNCTIVE (warning/threat)

More forceful than simple SI:
→ Como llegues tarde, te quedarás sin postre
(If you arrive late, you'll go without dessert)
→ Como no estudies, suspenderás
(If you don't study, you'll fail - strong warning)

✏️ DE + INFINITIVE (formal/literary)

Replaces SI clauses in formal writing:
→ De tener tiempo, iría contigo
(If I had time, I would go with you)
→ Formal alternative to 'Si tuviera tiempo...'

→ De haberlo sabido, no habría venido
(If I had known it, I wouldn't have come)
→ Formal alternative to 'Si lo hubiera sabido...'

Generally in literature/formal contexts

💡 IMPLIED CONDITIONS (without SI)

Condition implied rather than stated:
→ Con más dinero, viajaría más
(With more money, I would travel more)
→ Implies 'if I had more money'

→ En tu lugar, yo no iría
(In your place, I wouldn't go)
→ Implies 'if I were in your place'

🔗 OTHER CONDITIONAL PATTERNS:

• A no ser que (unless)
• En caso de que (in case)
• Con tal de que (provided that)

All require subjunctive and express conditions

questions.question: What tense follows SI in real conditions?
questions.hint: Real conditions: SI + PRESENT indicative. Example: Si llueve (present), no iré.

questions.question: 'Si llueve, no iré' - Is this real or hypothetical?
questions.hint: Present indicative (llueve) = real condition. It might actually rain; this is a real possibility.

questions.question: 'Si lloverá mañana, no iré' - Is this correct?

answers.text: No - never use future after SI, use present: Si llueve
Yes - future after SI is correct
Yes - but only in formal Spanish

questions.hint: NEVER use future tense after SI. Always use present for future conditions: Si llueve (not lloverá).

questions.question: 'Si estudias, aprobarás' - What tense is 'aprobarás'?
questions.hint: Aprobarás = future tense (you will pass). Common pattern: Si + present, future.

questions.question: 'Si tengo tiempo, leo' - What does this express?

answers.text: Habitual action (whenever I have time, I read)

questions.hint: Si + present, present = habitual action. Whenever this happens, that happens.

questions.question: 'Si ves a Juan, dile hola' - What form is 'dile'?
questions.hint: Pattern: Si + present, imperative. If you see Juan, tell (command) him hello.

questions.question: What pattern expresses hypothetical present conditions?
questions.hint: Hypothetical present: Si + imperfect subjunctive, conditional. Si tuviera, compraría.

questions.question: 'Si tuviera dinero, compraría un coche' - What does this mean?

answers.text: If I had money, I would buy a car (but I don't have money)
If I have money, I will buy a car (real possibility)
If I had had money, I would have bought a car (past)
When I have money, I buy a car (habitual)

questions.hint: Imperfect subjunctive (tuviera) + conditional (compraría) = hypothetical, contrary to present reality.

questions.question: 'Si fuera rico, viajaría' - Is the speaker rich?

answers.text: Was rich in past, not now

questions.hint: Si + imperfect subjunctive = contrary to fact. If I WERE rich (but I'm NOT), I would travel.

questions.question: 'Si tengo tiempo, voy' vs 'Si tuviera tiempo, iría' - What's the difference?

answers.text: First is real possibility; second is hypothetical/I don't have time
First is past; second is present
No difference, both mean the same
First is formal; second is informal

questions.hint: TENGO = real possibility. TUVIERA = hypothetical/contrary to fact (I don't have time).

questions.question: 'Si Juan estuviera aquí, podría preguntarle' - Is Juan here?
questions.hint: Imperfect subjunctive (estuviera) = contrary to fact. If he WERE here (but he's NOT).

questions.question: 'Si pudiera volar, iría a la luna' - Can the speaker fly?

answers.text: Will be able to fly in future

questions.hint: Si pudiera (imperfect subjunctive) = hypothetical/impossible. If I COULD fly (but I can't).

questions.question: What pattern expresses past hypothetical conditions?
questions.hint: Past hypothetical: Si + pluperfect subjunctive, conditional perfect. Si hubiera estudiado, habría aprobado.

questions.question: 'Si hubiera estudiado, habría aprobado' - Did the speaker study?

answers.text: No (didn't study, didn't pass - past hypothetical)

questions.hint: Pluperfect subjunctive = didn't happen in past. If I HAD studied (but I didn't), I would have passed (but I didn't).

questions.question: 'Si hubieras venido, habrías conocido a María' - Did 'you' come?
questions.hint: Past hypothetical: If you HAD come (but you didn't), you would have met María (but you didn't).

questions.question: 'Si lo hubiera sabido, no habría ido' - What does this express?

answers.text: Regret (didn't know, went, now regrets it)

questions.hint: Past hypothetical often expresses regret. If I had known (but I didn't), I wouldn't have gone (but I did).

questions.question: How is pluperfect subjunctive formed?
questions.hint: Pluperfect subjunctive: hubiera/hubiese estudiado (had studied - subjunctive form).

questions.question: How is conditional perfect formed?
questions.hint: Conditional perfect: habría aprobado (would have passed).

questions.question: 'Como llegues tarde, te quedarás sin postre' - What does COMO express?

answers.text: Warning/threat (if you arrive late - strong warning)

questions.hint: COMO + subjunctive = warning/threat. If you (dare) arrive late, consequences! More forceful than si.

questions.question: 'Como no estudies, suspenderás' - What mood after COMO?
questions.hint: COMO + subjunctive for warnings. Como no estudies (subjunctive) = If you don't study (warning).

questions.question: 'De tener tiempo, iría contigo' means...

answers.text: If I had time, I would go with you (formal/literary)
From having time, I would go with you
To have time, I would go with you
Of time, I would go with you

questions.hint: DE + infinitive = formal alternative to si clause. De tener = Si tuviera (If I had).

questions.question: 'De haberlo sabido, no habría venido' - What does DE express?
questions.hint: DE + perfect infinitive = formal 'if' for past hypotheticals. De haberlo sabido = Si lo hubiera sabido.

questions.question: 'Con más dinero, viajaría más' - Where is the condition?
questions.hint: Implied condition. Con más dinero = (Si tuviera) más dinero (If I had more money).

questions.question: 'En tu lugar, yo no iría' - What condition is implied?

answers.text: If I were in your place (but I'm not)

questions.hint: Implied condition: En tu lugar = Si yo estuviera en tu lugar (If I were in your place).
